security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, Chinese UTF-8 documentation, or security guidance text. No prompt injection, network behavior, secret access, or encoded binary content was found. The remaining concerns are path-scope enforcement in helper scripts and one instruction that can run an unbundled project-local Python entrypoint.

remediation.issue: Unbounded output paths in helper scripts
remediation.suggestion: Compare resolved output and root paths to the resolved project root before writing, and reject absolute paths outside that root.

remediation.issue: Unbundled project-init command can execute project-local code
remediation.suggestion: Remove the command, bundle the referenced script, or require explicit user confirmation before running project-local entrypoints.

remediation.issue: Hidden context files may capture sensitive task notes
remediation.suggestion: Add clear .gitignore guidance for .ai_context and remind users not to store credentials or customer data in logs.

semantic_findings.title: Path Scope Is Not Fully Enforced
semantic_findings.description: The helper scripts accept --out and --root path parameters and resolve them, but they do not enforce that writes stay under the active project root. An agent following untrusted task text could write a plan or .ai_context file outside the intended repository.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The write paths are directly controlled by CLI parameters and no project-root containment check compares them to the current repository. The issue requires command execution with chosen arguments, so severity is medium rather than high.

content.value_statement: AI-assisted projects lose decisions, constraints, and verification steps across sessions. This skill adds a lightweight memory file, mini plans, and append-only logs for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation and use of .ai_context/03_ACTIVE_TASK.md for the current mission and append-only logs.
Provides a Python logger that creates .ai_context and appends structured development entries.
Provides a Python planner that outputs goals, constraints, steps, and validation checks.
Explains slash-first manifest dispatch with optional cognitive skill behavior.
Includes concise references for mini TDD, debugging, and transparent collaboration.
limitations: It is a workflow guide, not a complete project management system.
The helper scripts use local files and do not sanitize note content.
File writes should be reviewed before use in sensitive repositories.
The main skill and references are mostly in Simplified Chinese.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a new repository
use_cases.description: Create a small active task file, capture goals, and plan the first verified steps before coding.

use_cases.title: Port an existing AI workflow
use_cases.description: Map a current project into .ai_context and manifest-driven commands without adopting the full AI Architecture protocol.

use_cases.title: Keep auditable work notes
use_cases.description: Append concise action, change, outcome, and next-step entries after each verified development step.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Mini Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use AI Architect Lite to turn this goal into a mini plan: [goal]. Include constraints, no more than five steps, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Project Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up the active task context for this repository. Summarize the current mission, owner, state, notes, and first log entry.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Verified Step
prompt_templates.prompt: Append a development log entry for this completed step: [step]. Include changes, outcome, verification result, and next action.

prompt_templates.title: Review Manifest Dispatch
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the current manifest workflow and propose a slash-first dispatch plan. Note missing commands, risks, and validation checks before changes.

output_examples.input: Goal: add a login flow to a small application.
output_examples.output: A mini plan with the goal, key constraints, three implementation steps, and a validation checklist before coding starts.

output_examples.input: Completed: created the active task file and verified the project structure.
output_examples.output: A concise log entry that records the action, changed files, verification result, and next planned step.

output_examples.input: Review our current AI workflow before migrating it.
output_examples.output: A short workflow assessment that explains memory files, slash-first dispatch, missing safeguards, and recommended next actions.

best_practices: Review every path before approving helper script writes.
Keep credentials, tokens, and customer data out of .ai_context logs.
Run or define validation before recording work as complete.
anti_patterns: Letting an agent write task files without confirming the repository root.
Using development logs as storage for secrets or private data.
Treating generated plans as final decisions without human review.

faq.question: Does this skill require network access?
faq.answer: No. The included helpers use Python standard library features and local files only.

faq.question: Will it modify my repository?
faq.answer: It can create or update .ai_context/03_ACTIVE_TASK.md when you run the logger. Review paths before approving writes.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, but command approval depends on your environment.

faq.question: Is it a full AI Architecture implementation?
faq.answer: No. It is a lightweight subset for memory, planning, dispatch notes, and structured logs.

faq.question: What should I avoid storing in logs?
faq.answer: Do not store secrets, API keys, passwords, or private customer data in .ai_context.

faq.question: What language are the instructions in?
faq.answer: The main skill and references are mostly Simplified Chinese. The README includes Chinese and English sections.
